choices.reason: Aminobenzonitrile measured 40.6/98.4 mL at 5/1, far above its prior prediction. The 2/1 prediction is 17.8/39.0 mL; this locates where the steep response begins under matched loading conditions.
The 0/1 aminobenzonitrile prediction is 4.4/12.0 mL. Together with the 2/1 choice and measured 5/1 result, it tests whether the large prior error persists under strong eluent.
Phenylpyridine measured 46.4/103.3 mL at 50/1, substantially later than predicted. This 10/1 point uses the same 150 µL loading and tests the lower-ratio part of that possible model blind spot.
The 20/1 phenylpyridine prediction is 25.5/47.0 mL. It adds an intermediate ratio before the measured 50/1 endpoint; loading differs, so the ratio comparison has that limitation.
Methylquinoline measured 51.3/108.5 mL at 10/1 versus a prior prediction of 24.2/55.1 mL. The 5/1 prediction of 34.4/66.6 mL tests whether the error extends to a stronger eluent.
The oxime measured V2 of 119.2 mL at 50/1, 36.3 mL above its prior prediction. Measuring the 20/1 prediction of 35.5/85.8 mL tests where its large elution interval develops.

Methoxybenzophenone was later than predicted at both 20/1 and 50/1, unlike several methoxy aromatics that were earlier than predicted. Its 5/1 result tests where this molecule's error changes with eluent strength.
Trimethoxybenzene was earlier than predicted at 2/1 and 5/1. The 50/1 prediction is 13.3/22.4 mL; measuring it tests whether this error persists into a PE-rich regime.
Cyclopropyl β-ketoester measured 6.3/11.9 mL at 1/1 and 44.5/81.2 mL at 20/1, the latter far above its prior prediction. This 5/1 point helps locate the rise alongside the pending 10/1 result.
The tert-butyl β-ketoester measured only 11.4/24.2 mL at 10/1 versus 23.2/46.9 mL predicted. Its 20/1 prediction of 23.1/48.0 mL tests whether that opposite-signed error persists at higher PE.

Iodobenzoate measured an unusually early V1 of 5.1 mL but V2 of 29.3 mL at 50/1 and 150 µL. This 50 µL experiment tests loading dependence of that wide interval; the current prediction is 12.1/27.0 mL.

Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde measured 6.9/23.0 mL at 5/1. The 20/1 prediction of 16.6/41.1 mL tests its solvent-ratio rise; a para isomer at 20/1 eluted much later, but different loading conditions limit that comparison.

The brominated carboxylic acid has a 50/1 prediction of 29.9/67.7 mL. It probes a strongly interacting acid motif at high PE; no direct measured support is supplied, so this is an exploratory chemical-prior choice.

Naphthylmethanol is predicted at 4.9/24.8 mL under 0/1 eluent. Its predicted elution width is large; comparison with pending benzyl alcohol measurements can test transfer across aromatic size, though the molecules differ.
Nitrobenzophenone at 1/1 and a 1000 µL loading-solvent volume is predicted at 7.9/20.7 mL. This tests a polar diaryl ketone under a large loading volume; direct same-molecule evidence is absent.
The oxime's 2/1 prediction is 9.1/19.3 mL. Paired with 20/1 and the measured 50/1 result, it distinguishes a gradual rise from a high-PE increase in V2 and elution width.

hypotheses.content: The earlier steep-retention prediction for diethyl malonate is contradicted across measured 5/1, 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1 conditions: all V1 values are 4.1–5.9 mL and V2 values are 5.8–7.9 mL. Its phenyl-substituted analogue is much later under PE-rich eluent, so that analogue did not transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: What structural feature separates the early unsubstituted malonate from the retained phenyl-substituted analogue?

hypotheses.content: The small fluorobenzoate V2 reversal from 5/1 to 10/1 remains observed: 12.71 versus 12.31 mL at matched loading. Its 0.40 mL size leaves the broader curve shape uncertain.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Would another loading amount reproduce this small local V2 difference?

hypotheses.content: The earlier methyl benzoylformate high-ratio plateau hypothesis remains contradicted: measured V2 rises from 33.3 mL at 20/1 to 62.0 mL at 50/1, while prior predictions stayed near 29 mL.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At which intermediate PE/EA ratio does its high-ratio V2 rise accelerate?

hypotheses.content: Anthranilate's measured V1/V2 increase from about 9/17 mL at 5/1 to 34.0/75.2 mL at 50/1, supporting the earlier solvent-ratio hypothesis. The premeasurement model captured 10/1 closely but underpredicted 50/1.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does a related anthranilate exhibit the same high-ratio increase?

hypotheses.content: Cyanobenzophenone rises sharply with PE-rich eluent: measured V1/V2 are 5.1/21.3 mL at 5/1, 7.7/31.6 at 10/1, 19.7/55.7 at 20/1 and 57.9/117.9 at 50/1. Prior predictions were too late at 5/1 and 10/1 yet too early at 50/1, showing a misplaced nonlinear response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where between 20/1 and 50/1 does its measured V2 increase most sharply?

hypotheses.content: Nitroacetophenone still directly supports a large ratio response: measured V1/V2 are 3.9/11.7 mL at 0/1 and 25.6/55.1 mL at 10/1. The prior 10/1 V2 prediction was too high.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does an intermediate ratio show a smooth or abrupt increase?

hypotheses.content: Ring-nitrogen effects are strongly structure and condition dependent. Phenylpyridine at 50/1, quinoline at 10/1 and methylquinoline at 10/1 were much later than predicted; dimethylpyridine at 5/1 and 10/1 was earlier than predicted. A blanket ring-nitrogen correction is unsupported.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At intermediate ratios, which ring-nitrogen scaffolds retain the late-elution underprediction?

hypotheses.content: The multifunctional ester was predicted fairly closely at 2/1 but its V2 was underpredicted at 5/1 and 10/1. The amino-substituted unsaturated ester was overpredicted at 10/1 under DCM loading but underpredicted at 20/1 under PE loading; that contrast cannot be assigned to PE/EA ratio alone.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Under matched loading solvent and volume, where does each molecule's V2 prediction error change size or sign?

hypotheses.content: Large high-PE V2 underpredictions for two phenols remain a subset-specific observation. The phenolic aldehyde at 50/1 was predicted closely, while its measured 0/1 V2 was 13.7 mL versus 20.2 mL predicted; a related bromohydroxybenzaldehyde at 0/1 was also somewhat earlier than predicted.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which phenol substitutions and eluent ratios produce the large underpredicted V2 values?

hypotheses.content: The β-ketoester results now show opposite error directions across substitutions: cyclopropyl β-ketoester was underpredicted at 20/1, tert-butyl acetoacetate was overpredicted at 10/1, and the benzyl-substituted β-ketoester at 20/1 was predicted closely. Structural transfer is therefore uncertain.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do intermediate and higher ratios preserve the opposite error directions for cyclopropyl and tert-butyl variants?

hypotheses.content: Bromomethyl benzoate V1/V2 rose from measured 5.4/11.5 mL at 1/1 and 7.0/16.5 at 5/1 to 22.3/43.5 at 50/1. The prior 50/1 prediction of 20.2/36.7 mL was moderately early, so the broad trend transferred better than in several other classes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does an intermediate-ratio measurement follow a smooth rise?

hypotheses.content: Methoxy aromatic prediction errors differ with structure: trimethoxybenzene and dimethoxytoluene were earlier than predicted at 2/1–5/1, while methoxybenzophenone was later than predicted at 20/1 and 50/1. A carbonyl-associated difference is plausible but confounded by ratio and scaffold.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At a matched 5/1 ratio, does methoxybenzophenone remain later than predicted while trimethoxybenzene remains earlier?

hypotheses.content: The aminobenzonitrile at 5/1 was much later than predicted, whereas non-aminated methylbenzonitriles were earlier than predicted at 10/1–50/1. Amino substitution may change retention and interval width, but these observations also differ in ratios and substitution patterns.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How early or late is aminobenzonitrile at matched 0/1 and 2/1 settings?

hypotheses.content: Iodobenzoate at 50/1 and 150 µL had an unusually early V1 of 5.1 mL and a later V2 of 29.3 mL, both much earlier than its prior predictions. Whether sample loading amount affects this broad interval is untested.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 50 µL measurement preserve the early V1 and broad V2−V1 interval?

hypotheses.content: The oxime at 50/1 measured 43.1/119.2 mL, with V2 substantially later than its prior 82.9 mL prediction. Lower-ratio response is unmeasured, so the onset of its broad interval is unknown.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1 and 20/1, how quickly does measured V2 and the V2−V1 interval increase?

feedback_interpretation: Round-one measurements exposed large, opposite-signed errors within broad chemical labels: several ring-nitrogen compounds were later than predicted while dimethylpyridine was earlier; methoxy aromatics were often early while methoxybenzophenone was late; cyclopropyl and tert-butyl β-ketoesters differed; aminobenzonitrile was very late while methylbenzonitriles were early. I selected matched-molecule ratio points to locate these changes, plus a 50/1 loading contrast for iodobenzoate. The diethyl malonate 5/1 result confirmed consistently early elution, so I did not spend another choice on that saturated series.
